newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Country Heights shrs up on township news.
newsitem.headline: Country Heights shrs up on township news.

text.p: The stock and warrants of property firm Country Heights Bhd surged on news that the company is involved in a high-technology township project, analysts and brokers said.
The company announced on Wednesday that it would be jointly developing the Cyberjaya high-technology township, which is expected to cost 23.8 billion ringgit.
Just ahead of the lunch break, the shares were up 1.60 ringgit at 19.00 ringgit.

The warrants, with a conversion price of 5.30 ringgit, were up 70 cents at 7.70 ringgit. Converting one warrant at the current price will give a conversion rate of 13 ringgit, a six ringgit discount to the stock price.
"Today the warrants are catching up with the mother shares, but the mother shares are also moving," Mohaiyani Securities' head of research, Audrey Ho.
But some analysts said the play on Country Heights may be overdone as Cyberjaya will be jointly developed by seven companies, one businessman and the Selangor state government.
"Country Heights has an effective 13.7 percent stake," Ho said.
